current_answer: For an existing-system dashboard, start with the actual user decision, data, components, tokens, and required empty, loading, and error states in a project brief. Do not add a design-skill stack by default. If the agent still needs a dashboard-specific workflow, PracticalSwan Frontend Design 2.0 is a conditional candidate; use Anthropic Frontend Design when visual identity is genuinely open, and Vercel Web Design Guidelines for a later file review. These are source-based routes, not tested outcomes. All sixteen listings still lack a pool-run no-skill comparison.

catalogue_card.question: Which skill should you use for a dashboard?
catalogue_card.text: If the dashboard already has components and tokens, start with a project brief and no extra skill. PracticalSwan Frontend Design 2.0 is a conditional next trial for data clarity and missing states. We have not tested it against the no-skill route.

summary: Start an existing-system dashboard with its user decision, real data, units, freshness, components, and required states.
PracticalSwan Frontend Design 2.0 is a conditional dashboard candidate; Anthropic Frontend Design fits when visual identity is open.
Use Vercel Web Design Guidelines for a named-file review after implementation, not as proof of the rendered result.
Compare one skill with the same careful no-skill brief before claiming improvement.
uncertainty: A fresh dashboard request is one user report, not measured demand.
The task routes come from pinned instructions; this pool has not installed or tested these skills on a dashboard.
